compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
## Problem

RealGitHost.commit_and_push clones the target repository with a bare `git clone <remote> <work>`. That pulls every branch and the full blob history even though the function needs exactly one ref. Against an established repository the transfer overruns the five-minute startToCloseTimeout the draft pull request workflow gives the commit activity.

The overrun is not recoverable. GithubMediator._gated advances the Postgres sequence gate before the effect runs and records the ledger entry only on success, so a timed-out commit leaves the gate advanced and every Temporal retry raises StaleActionError. The maximumAttempts of 3 is dead in this path.

## Evidence

Measured inside the activity worker against the private remote with the injected token.

- Full clone, 35 seconds, 1.1 GB
- `--single-branch`, 40 seconds, 1.1 GB
- `--filter=blob:none --single-branch`, 17 seconds, 239 MB

Branch narrowing alone does not help because the repository is a single large pack. Omitting blobs is what cuts the transfer. Disk was not the constraint, 55 GB free.

Two massgov pilot runs failed this way. Worker logs show the clone at git_host.py:124 holding for the entire 300 second budget before cancellation. `_git` at git_host.py:84 runs subprocess with no timeout, so the thread outlives the activity and the clone keeps running after Temporal has given up.

`ensure_branch`, directly above `commit_and_push` in the same class, already clones with `--branch --single-branch`. `commit_and_push` is the outlier.

## Approach

Move the existing `_ls_remote` branch probe above the clone so the ref to fetch is known before the transfer starts, then clone exactly that ref with blobs filtered out.

Ref resolution has two cases and the probe already distinguishes them. When `_ls_remote` finds `request.branch` on the remote the clone takes `--branch <request.branch>`. When it does not, the clone takes `--branch <request.base>` and the existing `checkout -b <request.branch>` below creates the branch in the work tree exactly as it does today. The `branch_exists` result is computed once and drives both decisions, so the clone ref and the checkout stay consistent.

A blobless clone is safe here. The only history the function reads is commit messages, which it walks with `git log --grep` for the trailer idempotency check. It reads no blob. Blobs for the checkout are fetched on demand by the working tree materialisation.

Separately, raise the commit activity budget through a single named constant used by both the commit and the CI repair call sites.

The 15 minute value is derived from the measurements above. The blobless clone moves the transfer from 35 seconds to 17 seconds at rest, but the observed failures held the full 300 second budget, so contention inflated a 35 second clone by at least 8.6 times. Applying that same observed inflation factor to the 17 second blobless clone gives roughly 150 seconds, and 15 minutes is six times that, leaving headroom for the commit, the trailer search, and the push that follow the clone inside the same activity. The value is chosen to be generous rather than tight because the failure mode is unrecoverable, not merely slow, so a false timeout costs an entire run while a long ceiling costs only a delayed failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `commit_and_push` calls `_ls_remote` for `request.branch` before it clones, and the clone argument vector carries `--filter=blob:none`, `--single-branch`, and `--branch` with the resolved ref. Proved by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py::test_a_commit_clones_only_the_ref_it_needs`.
- [ ] When the branch does not yet exist on the remote the clone uses `request.base` and the branch is still created in the work tree, so a first commit on a new branch behaves as it does today. Proved by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py::test_commit_and_push_is_idempotent_via_the_execution_trailer`.
- [ ] The trailer idempotency check still finds an existing trailer against a blobless clone, so a repeated commit returns the prior sha without committing again. Proved by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py -k trailer`.
- [ ] The commit activity call site reads the shared `_COMMIT_TIMEOUT` constant. Checked by `grep -n "commit_timeout = _COMMIT_TIMEOUT" services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py` returning exactly two lines.
- [ ] No `commit_timeout = timedelta(minutes=5)` literal remains. Checked by `grep -n "commit_timeout = timedelta(minutes=5)" services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py` returning nothing. The unrelated `model_timeout` and `gather_repo_context` five-minute literals in the same file are untouched.
- [ ] The push, the trailer text, and the returned commit sha are unchanged. Proved by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py`.
- [ ] The change introduces no lint regression. Proved by `ruff check .`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py` covers the commit path against a bare local remote, the trailer idempotency check, the new-branch case, and the new clone argument assertion.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py` covers the workflow activity options that carry the timeout.
- `ruff check .` covers lint.
- The full suite is the regression net, since the timeout constant is read by two workflow paths.

## Out of scope

The sequence gate retry-masking defect itself. It is what makes this timeout fatal rather than slow, but fixing the gate ordering changes the ordering of every gated GitHub side effect and belongs in its own change.

Adding a subprocess timeout to `_git`. The missing timeout is what lets the clone thread outlive a cancelled activity, but `_git` is the shared helper behind every git call in this adapter, so giving it a deadline changes the failure behaviour of clone, push, log, config, and checkout alike. This ticket bounds the exposure instead, because the orphaned clone now transfers 239 MB rather than 1.1 GB into a temporary directory that is discarded when it finishes.

file_impact.reason: Move the _ls_remote branch probe above the clone and narrow the clone to --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch <ref>
Add _COMMIT_TIMEOUT and use it at both the commit and CI repair activity call sites
Assert the clone argument vector carries the single-branch, blobless, and resolved branch flags
